sentences.text: Before dwelling into analyzing the disputed facts in issue it is relevant to have the birds eye of the case of petitioners in a nutshell.

. It is the case of petitioners that, on 12.12.2016 at about 8.00 a.m, the deceased was proceeding as an occupant in Indica Car bearing No.KA-07-5981 along with Keerthiprakash, Boraiah and Nandish which was driving by one Mr. Sathish on NH-44 road, Dharmathupatti, when they reached near VAO office, Pothudoddi village, at that time, the driver of TNSTC Bus bearing Reg.No.TN-58-N-2169 came in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed to the car in which deceased was traveling.
Due to the terrific impact the deceased and other inmates of the car have sustained grievous injuries.

Soon after the accident, all were shifted to Dindigul Government hospital, and thereafter deceased was shifted to KIMS hospital, Bengaluru wherein he took treatment at intensive care till 18.12.2016, but in spite of better medical treatment the deceased succumbed to injuries on 18.12.2016.

It is submitted that the petitioners have spent Rs.3,00,000/-
towards hospitalization, conveyance, medical treatment, attendant and other incidental expenses of the deceased.
It is further submitted that because of death of deceased the claimants have suffered both financially and emotionally.

It is submitted that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, he was running transport office and also working as Driver and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- p.m. and bata of Rs.300/- per day, and because of untimely death of deceased, the petitioners have suffered economically as well as emotionally.

It is contended that the accident happened SCCH-23 MVC-128/2018 because of rash and negligent driving of the drivers of Bus and car and as such all the respondents No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence prayed to allow the petition.

14. In order to substantiate the contentions of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 stepped into the witness box and filed her affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P15 documents.

On the other hand in order to substantiate the defence of the respondent No.1 and 3 and to demolish the case of the petitioners, the respondent No.1 and 3 counsel have cross examined PW.1 at length distinctly.
15. On the other hand, repelling to the contentions urged by the petitioners, the respondent No. 1 has attacked the case of the petitioners on various prisms known to fact and law.
The first limb of contention urged by the respondent No.1 is that the accident happened due to rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Tata Indica Car i.e., respondent No.2 car.
It is also positively asserted that, driver of the said Car was not possessing valid DL at the time of accident and the said car does not have valid permit and FC.
Further denied all the allegations made in the petition.

16. Per contra, the respondent No.3 has also filed written statement urging various contentions known to fact and law.
The first squirt defence is that, the charge sheet is filed as against the driver of the TNSTC bus as such there is absolutely no negligence on the part of the respondent No.2 car driver.

The next plank of defence of the respondent No.3 is that the respondent No.2 car was covered under the liability only policy and the respondent No.3 cannot indemnify for the death of the deceased as the deceased is the third party.
In support of these contentions the respondent No.3 got examined its administrative officer of legal department as RW.3 and got marked Ex.R.3 and R4 documents.
17. Previously, the respondent No.3 had examined its erstwhile administrative officer as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 documents.
After restoration of this case respondent No.1 had recalled RW.1, but RW.1 could not tender himself for cross-examination.

On dissection of materials placed on record, after marshaling of facts in issue and after hearing erudite counsel appearing for combating parties, this Tribunal opines that this issue is pregmented with inner issues such as :
1) Whether there is any composite negligence on the part of the driver of the respondent No.2-car also?
2) Whether the accident had happened because of the sole negligence on the part of the respondent No.1-bus driver?
19.
The first moot question to be considered is with regard to the factum of negligence.
It is a trite law that the the factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.

It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has Gowramma vs Tami Nadu State Transport Corporation on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39218642/
6 some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
SCCH-23 MVC-128/2018 The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.

sentences.text: Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
20. Reverting back to the factual matrix it is vociferously argued by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 counsel that even the driver of the car also negligence.
Hence some amount of contributory negligence may be taken.
Per contra the respondent No.3 counsel stoutly contended that there is no FIR and chargesheet is against the car driver.
As such the respondent No.2 and 3 cannot be made liable to pay compensation.

From these contentions canvassed by respondent No.1 counsel this court could cull out that the respondent No.1 is shirking its responsibility of paying SCCH-23 MVC-128/2018 compensation on respondent No.2 and 3.
In a way the respondent No.1 is contending that it is a case of composite negligence.
Now it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to the composite negligence.
The term Negligence means failure to exercise care towards others which a reasonable and prudent person would in a circumstance or taking action with such a reasonable person would not.
When the negligence of two or more persons results in the same damage to a third person there is said to be a "composite negligence".

Furthermore, in the case of composite negligence, each wrongdoer is jointly liable to the injured for payment of the entire damages and the injured person has the choice of proceeding against any or all of them.

The law in such a case is that the claimant is entitled to sue all or any of them for the full amount of his loss and each is said to be jointly and severally liable for it;The composite tortfeasors are each jointly and severally liable.
No tortfeasor is permitted to argue that there should be an equitable distribution of blame and that his liability should only extend to the degree of his negligence.
21. Reverting back to the instant case, now let me analyze the documentary and oral evidence in the light of settled principles of law as to discover if there is any composite negligence.
The petitioners in order to prove the factum of negligence have mainly relied on Ex.P.1 to 6 documents.
It is needless to mention that, it is settled law of plethora of SCCH-23 MVC-128/2018 decisions that the factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
It is specifically contended by the petitioners that, there is a negligence on the part of the car and TNSTC bus driver.

On the other Gowramma vs Tami Nadu State Transport Corporation on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39218642/
7 hand the said allegations urged by petitioners is stoutly denied by the respondent No.1 herein.

sentences.text: There is absolutely no delay in setting criminal law into motion.

The accident had happened on 12.12.2016 at 8.00 a.m and the criminal law was set into motion at 4.00 p.m on 12.12.2016.
22.
One of the document Ex.P.2 & 3 being the Spot Mahazar and spot sketch.
On close perusal of spot sketch at Ex.P.3 it reveals that the accident on the left side of the lane of the car.
This categorically reveals that the TNSTC bus driver has gone extreme right side of his lane and dashed the oncoming car whose driver is going on the extreme left side of the road.
Further on perusal of these documents with astuteness it is clearly forthcoming that there is absolutely no negligence on the part of the car driver.
The respondent No.1 has also made an endeavor to examine the driver of the TNSTC as RW.2.
He in his chief-examination had deposed that the accident had happened because of the negligence on the part of the car driver.
When he was subjected to the litmus test of the cross-examination he categorically admitted that the charge sheet is filed against him.
This court is aware of the fact that the charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to the negligence.

But having regard to the Ex.P.2 and 3 being the spot mahazar and spot sketch it is clearly emanating that the SCCH-23 MVC-128/2018 respondent No.1 bus driver had gone completely right side to his lane and dashed the oncoming car which is on its left side.
Further Ex.P.3 discloses that the accident had happened in the straight road.
If the respondent No.1 bus driver was coming in a normal speed then he would have certainly avoided the accident.
Coming to the extreme right side of his lane and dashing the oncoming car is the shear negligence on the part of the respondent No.1 bus driver.
23. Much was made hill out of a mole by the respondent No.1 counsel contended that IMV report was not filed by the petitioner.

Merely on the fact that the IMV report was not filed by the petitioner,
the whole version of the petitioner cannot be distrusted.
It is not in dispute that the car was involved in the accident.
Further it is also not in dispute that the respondent No.1 bus is involved in the accident.
It is also not the case of the respondent No.1 TNSTC that the respondent No.1 bus was facing the technical or mechanical defects as on the time of the accident.

When such being the case,
the mere non-production of the IMV report is not at all fatal to the case of the petitioners.
24. Further more even the chargesheet as per Ex.P.5 was also filed as against the driver of the bus.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.2 & 3 coupled with Ex.P.5 chargesheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence of the bus driver.
Further more when this court goes through the cross examination of RW.3 it SCCH-23 MVC-128/2018 is clearly forthcoming that, the chargesheet was not challenged.

When such is the case and in the absence of any proof, the version of petitioners coupled with other documentary proof has to be trusted.
25.

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
27. ISSUE NO.2:
The petitioners claim that, petitioners are the mother and brother of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit-in-lieu of her chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhar cards, marked at Ex's.P.10 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
The evidence discloses that deceased is the son who is a one of the bread winner to the family and as such the petitioner No.1 was dependent on deceased.

It is pertinent to note that,
this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased SCCH-23 MVC-128/2018 has not been disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representative of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heirs of deceased.
Further when its comes to the dependency of the petitioner No.2, it is relevant to note that the petitioner No.2 is the brother of the deceased.
Petitioner No.2 is major.

Added more there is nothing placed on record before the court that the petitoner No.2 was the dependient of the earning of the deceased when such being the case he cannot be considered as a dependent on the deceased.
28. In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- on the death of deceased Sathyakumar C.S. in the road traffic accident.

It is specifically urged by the petitioners that, deceased was hale and healthy, he was running Transport office and also working as Driver and doing business and thereby earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- p.m. and the bata of Rs.300/- per day.
In order to substantiate the said fact the petitioners have not produced any documents to prove the same.

sentences.text: It is trite law that, SCCH-23 MVC-128/2018 when the petitioners have failed to prove the income, the income of the deceased has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
30. The next moot question to be considered is as to how the notional income has to be considered in the eye of law.

The learned counsel for the respondent argued vociferously by relying on the decision of the Hon'ble High court of Division Bench in MFA No.7404/2014 dated 06.12.2022 in the case of Smt. Mariyamma W/o. Hucchellappa & others V/s Suyambulingam.V & anr.

In the above said decision it was held that, the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority,
Bengaluru cannot be considered, the minimum wages under Minimum Wages Act has to be taken into consideration, because the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority,
Bengaluru override statutory guidelines.

By relying on this decision it is argued strenuously by the learned counsel for the respondent that, the notional income as fixed by Karnataka Legal Service Authority, cannot be taken into consideration and the court must dwell in to considering the notional income as prescribed under Minimum Wages Act.
31.

Per Contra the petitioners counsel during the course of arguments has relied on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) SCCH-23 MVC-128/2018 dated.05.07.2023.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
32.
It is pertinent to note that, the Subordinate courts are governed under as per Article 141 of Indian Constitution which deals with law of precedents.
The decision relied by the respondent counsel is rendered by the Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the month of December- 2022.
The decision which is relied by the petitioner counsel is rendered by the Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the month of July-2023.

As per the principles laid down by the plethora of decisions by Constitutional Courts it would be culled out in two decisions taking contradictory view by the Division Bench then recent one will prevail over the SCCH-23 MVC-128/2018 previous one.
When such is the case law rendered by the Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) rendered in the month of July-2023 is binding on this tribunal.
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 14.11.2016.

Therefore, Rs.9,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly Gowramma vs Tami Nadu State Transport Corporation on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39218642/
10 income of the deceased.

sentences.text: 33. The petitioners have produced the Aadhar card and DL of the deceased to show his age as per Ex.P10 and 11.

The contents ingrained in the Aadhar card and DL of the deceased discloses the date of birth as 13.07.1990 and the accident had taken place on 12.12.2016 and it shows that, at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 26 years.

Hence the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '17'.
34.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage of future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent SCCH-23 MVC-128/2018 Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 26 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased was aged about 26 years and as such, 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.13,300/- p.m. (Rs.9,500/- + 3,800/- i.e., 40%).

35. Further as stated above that, deceased was a bachelor, as per the decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla verma V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation, the 50% of the income of the deceased shall be deducted towards his personal expenses as the deceased unmarried, thereby the 50% income of the deceased has to be deducted for his personal expenditure.

entities.text: Sarla verma V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
On such deduction,
the income of the deceased comes to Rs.6,650/- p.m. (Rs.13,300/- X 50/100).
36. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.6,650/- p.m. and the multiplier "17" is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.13,56,600/- (Rs.6,650 X 12 X 17)
Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.13,56,600/- under the head of loss of dependency.
37. In this case, petitioner No.1 is the mother of the deceased and

as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu SCCH-23 MVC-128/2018 Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu SCCH-23 MVC-128/2018 Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose of their child during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their oral in the family unit.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.40,000/- under the head of Filial consortium.

38. Further, as law laid down by the Hon'ble Appex court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to the estate, funeral expenses and consortium to be awarded.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
The first squirt defence is that, the charge sheet is filed as against the driver of the TNSTC bus as such there is absolutely no negligence on the part of the respondent No.2 car driver.
It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The next plank of defence of the respondent No.3 is that the respondent No.2 car was covered under the liability only policy and the respondent No.3 cannot indemnify for the death of the deceased as the deceased is the third party.
It is a trite law that the the factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
In a way the respondent No.1 is contending that it is a case of composite negligence.
The term Negligence means failure to exercise care towards others which a reasonable and prudent person would in a circumstance or taking action with such a reasonable person would not.
When the negligence of two or more persons results in the same damage to a third person there is said to be a "composite negligence".
Furthermore, in the case of composite negligence, each wrongdoer is jointly liable to the injured for payment of the entire damages and the injured person has the choice of proceeding against any or all of them.
The law in such a case is that the claimant is entitled to sue all or any of them for the full amount of his loss and each is said to be jointly and severally liable for it;The composite tortfeasors are each jointly and severally liable.
It is needless to mention that, it is settled law of plethora of SCCH-23 MVC-128/2018 decisions that the factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
It is specifically contended by the petitioners that, there is a negligence on the part of the car and TNSTC bus driver.
There is absolutely no delay in setting criminal law into motion.
When he was subjected to the litmus test of the cross-examination he categorically admitted that the charge sheet is filed against him.
This court is aware of the fact that the charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to the negligence.
But having regard to the Ex.P.2 and 3 being the spot mahazar and spot sketch it is clearly emanating that the SCCH-23 MVC-128/2018 respondent No.1 bus driver had gone completely right side to his lane and dashed the oncoming car which is on its left side.
Merely on the fact that the IMV report was not filed by the petitioner,
the whole version of the petitioner cannot be distrusted.
It is not in dispute that the car was involved in the accident.
It is also not the case of the respondent No.1 TNSTC that the respondent No.1 bus was facing the technical or mechanical defects as on the time of the accident.
When such being the case,
the mere non-production of the IMV report is not at all fatal to the case of the petitioners.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.2 & 3 coupled with Ex.P.5 chargesheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence of the bus driver.
Further more when this court goes through the cross examination of RW.3 it SCCH-23 MVC-128/2018 is clearly forthcoming that, the chargesheet was not challenged.
When such is the case and in the absence of any proof, the version of petitioners coupled with other documentary proof has to be trusted.
